about: The memory the stages of a whole build reached, measured in a from-scratch build of the whole game (its build-profile.json: peak_bytes = the stage's process tree at its peak, largest_process_bytes = its largest single process, workers = the most workers it ran). A failed build reads it when neither this build nor an earlier build of its workspace measured the stage (tools/build_failure.py, the advice a build prints when it stops for memory): a stage whose largest process holds most of its peak is not helped by fewer workers. The resource plan of a full build reads it the same way, as the last-resort measurement of a stage no earlier build of its workspace measured (tools/resource_plan.py gather: its memory only, not its time): stages whose peaks do not fit side by side run one after another, each with a WARN line. Stages under 1 GiB are left out. Measurements, not limits: nothing is built from this file, so no stage key reads it.
measured_in: the v0.0.66 from-scratch build of the whole game (16 November 2026, --jobs 20, 48 GiB given)
build_peak_note: the build's memory in use at its peak, the file cache not counted (build-progress.json), with the stages chim and chim-room-batches running side by side
